Brazil_Haiti_2026_06_19.recap_tekst:
Brazil beat Haiti 3-0.
Goals: Cunha (23, 36) and Vinicius Jr. (45+3).

Braziledged ahead of Morocco on goal difference at the top of Group C after a comfortable victory that ends Haiti's hopes of progressing.
The Manchester United forward lashed the ball into the top corner to double Brazil's lead.
It took over 20 minutes, but once they got going there was not stopping the five-time champions.
Vinicius Jr created the first goal by firing a shot that Johnny Placide couldn't hold on to.
Key stat: Matheus Cunha's first goal was just his second senior international goal for Brazil and his first at the World Cup. His double helped Brazil overtake Germany as the highest scoring country in World Cup history with 240 goals.

Ecuador_Curaçao_2026_06_20.recap_tekst:
Ecuador and Curaçao drew 0-0.
Ecuador hit the woodwork three times and had nearly 30 attempts, but were unable to find a way through the Caribbean side's defence.

Early on, the Blue Wave were able to take advantage of the space Ecuador left as they pushed for an opener.
As time wound down, Ecuador pressed even harder for a goal and Valencia nearly scored a strong header from a whipped in cross, only to be denied by Room.
Ecuadortook the game to Curaçao in Kansas City but the evening turned out to be an Eloy Room masterpiece.
Key stat: This is just the third goalless draw in 33 World Cup encounters between CONMEBOL and Concacaf nations. The other two were: Uruguay 0-0 Mexico-1966 group stage Brazil 0-0 Mexico-2014 group stage

Germany_Ivory_Coast_2026_06_20.recap_tekst:
Germany beat Ivory Coast 2-1.
Goals: Germany — Undav (68, 90+4); Ivory Coast — Kessie (30).

Deniz Undav emerged from the bench to score twice and send Germany through to the FIFA World Cup 2026™ Round of 32.
Emerse Fae's Côte d'Ivoire were on course to qualify after Franck Kessie's goal on the half hour, but Undav's close-range header and added-time goal proved enough to see the Germans advance at Toronto Stadium.
Germany almost carved out the perfect start when Kai Havertz won a header from kick-off and fired the loose ball just over the crossbar.
He called upon Nadiem Amiri and Undav on the hour and just eight minutes later the former sent an inch-perfect cross for the latter to head in the leveller.
Key stat: Deniz Undav now has nine goals from his last eight Germany caps.

Netherlands_Sweden_2026_06_20.recap_tekst:
Netherlands beat Sweden 5-1.
Goals: Netherlands — Brobbey (5, 17), Gakpo (47, 54) and Summerville (89); Sweden — Elanga (59).

The Netherlands have stormed to the summit of Group F after braces from Brian Brobbey and Cody Gakpo secured a thrilling victory over Sweden in Houston.
The Swedes contributed throughout to this enthralling encounter, but were playing catch-up from the moment Brobbey slammed home an inviting Gakpo cross inside five minutes.
Sweden piled on the pressure thereafter and thought they had a goal back only for the offside flag to curtail the celebrations that followed Gustaf Lagerbielke’s brave header.
Substitute Anthony Elanga offered Sweden some hope with a superb breakaway effort, but the impressive Crysencio Summerville restored the Oranje's four-goal cushion with an emphatic right-foot strike as the clock ticked down.
Key stat: Gakpo’s second goal was his fifth in only seven World Cup appearances. He is now just two behind the Netherlands’ record scorer at the finals, Johnny Rep.

Scotland_Morocco_2026_06_19.recap_tekst:
Morocco beat Scotland 1-0.
Goals: Saibari (2).

The victory leaves Morocco with four points and sitting atop Group C ahead of Brazil's game in Philadelphia.
Morocco took an early lead over Scotlandat Boston Stadium and never looked back.
The Atlas Lions' solitary goal came courtesy of Ismael Saibari, who ran past the Scottish back line, brought down a well-weighted ball from Brahim Diaz and slammed the ball past Angus Gunn and into the roof of the net.
Saibari's finish was a record breaker: the fastest so far at FIFA World Cup 2026™ and Morocco's fastest ever at the global showpiece.
Key stat: Ismael Saibari has become just the second African player to score in each of his first two appearances at the World Cup after Egypt's Mohamed Salah (against Russia and Saudi Arabia in 2018).

Tunisia_Japan_2026_06_20.recap_tekst:
Japan beat Tunisia 4-0.
Goals: Kamada (4), Ueda (31, 83) and Junya Ito (69).

The impressive Keito Nakamura was the architect, dancing into the box and squaring across the face of goal where Daichi Kamada was on hand to prod home through a troupe of blue and white shirts.
His opener was his second of the tournament and the fastest that Japan have scored at a World Cup.
Ayase Ueda doubled the lead on the half-hour, being allowed the space of the Sierra Madre to stride towards goal and lash home from the top of the box.
Parachuted into the job earlier in the week, new Tunisia coach Herve Renard was unable to orchestrate a response from the North African side and Japan went further ahead as Ueda turned provider, with Junya Ito slotting home a third midway through the second half.
Key stat: Daichi Kamada's fourth-minute goal is the fastest scored by a Japanese player in FIFA World Cup history. The previous quickest was Shinji Kagawa in 2018 against Colombia when he scored in the sixth minute.

Turkey_Paraguay_2026_06_19.recap_tekst:
Paraguay beat Turkey 1-0.
Goals: Matias Galarza (2).

Andres Cubas pinched possession and passed to Julio Enciso, who then released Matias Galarza to unleash a left-footed effort through the legs of Merih Demiral and past a diving Ugurcan Cakir.
With both nations coming off first-up defeats, a response was needed in this San Francisco showdown and it took Paraguay just 64 seconds to find one.
With Gustavo Alfaro’s side a goal up but a man down, the second half dynamic was very much Türkiye attack against Paraguay defence.
* Matias Galarza's goal after just 64 seconds was the fastest so far at the FIFA World Cup 2026
